title: DeepSeek leaves a ClickHouse database with chat history and secrets open to the internet
summary: Researchers found a ClickHouse database belonging to DeepSeek reachable from the internet with no authentication. Its log tables held more than a million lines, including chat history, API secrets, backend details and operational metadata, and the database's web interface accepted arbitrary SQL queries. DeepSeek secured the exposure promptly after being notified.
attack_vector: No attack needed: production log database exposed publicly without authentication
root_cause: Database service exposed on public hosts with no access control; logs stored chat content and secrets
impact: Over a million log lines with user chat history and API secrets readable by anyone; arbitrary queries could have allowed further access to the environment
detection_method: External security researchers mapping the vendor's internet-facing assets
